page: Microsoft Azure D8d_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DDv4 instance series. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at a base frequency of 2.6 GHz, the server allocates 8 dedicated vCPUs distributed across 4 physical cores via multithreading. It is built on the x86_64 architecture and incorporates modern instruction sets including AVX-512 and AVX-512 VNNI. System memory totals 32.0 GB, maintaining an even 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Local ephemeral storage is bundled as a 322 GB solid-state drive, while no hardware accelerators or GPUs are included.

Performance across synthetic and operational benchmarks generally aligns with mid-tier industry baselines. The system achieved a Geekbench multi-core score of 4751.0 alongside a single-core score of 1237.0, supported by a PassMark CPU score of 8537.82. Memory subsystems recorded 46.63 GB/sec in uncached read bandwidth and 34.22 GB/sec for sequential write operations. In workload-specific benchmarks, the server sustained 7.06 million Redis SET operations per second and 6.77 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Compression tasks reveal throughput bottlenecks, with single-threaded gzip and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression registering in the lower quartile.

The inclusion of direct local SSD storage offers operational value for workloads requiring rapid scratch disk space without incurring additional detached volume overhead. Because the 8 vCPUs share 4 physical cores, sustained thread contention can impact intensive compression tasks. The server delivers reliable resource density for standard application hosting, intermediate caching tiers, relational database engines, microservices, and continuous integration pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure D8d_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at 2.6 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores, 32.0 GB of system memory, and 322 GB of integrated local SSD storage without GPU acceleration. The balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory configuration delivers steady mid-tier performance across synthetic and application benchmarks, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 4751.0 and 7.06 million Redis SET operations per second. While vector instruction support is present via AVX-512, multithreaded data compression tasks show weaker throughput relative to peers. With bundled local storage and balanced resource allocation, the D8d_v4 represents a practical platform for web serving, microservices, database operations, and development pipelines requiring fast local scratch disks.
